svg.title: SQL Server on Azure VMs with an availability group, backup and disaster recovery
svg.desc: A two-region design for SQL Server installed on Azure virtual machines: an Always On availability group across two availability zones with a load balancer listener and cloud witness, an asynchronous replica in a second region, Azure Backup to a Recovery Services vault, and Site Recovery for the app tier. A free-form drawing with 15 outlined areas: Region 1 (primary); Virtual network 1; App subnet; SQL subnet (one subnet across both zones); Availability zone 1; SQL Server on Azure VM; Availability zone 2; SQL Server on Azure VM; Region 2 (disaster recovery); Virtual network 2; App subnet; SQL subnet; SQL Server on Azure VM; Key. It holds 23 labelled items joined by 15 black arrows; dashed arrows are optional, standby or asynchronous paths. Arrow labels: Connect to the listener name; Synchronous commit, automatic failover; Asynchronous commit, manual failover; Stream-based backup straight to the vault; Quorum vote; Azure Site Recovery replication; AG fails over first; Traffic or data path; Asynchronous or manual; Two-way replication. Green numbered circles on arrows match the numbered notes under the drawing.

text.tspan: SQL subnet (one subnet across both zones)
Clients reach the app tier VM in the app subnet of virtual network 1.
The app connects to the availability group listener name. With the SQL Server VMs in a single subnet, an Azure internal load balancer holds the listener IP address, and each region needs its own load
balancer. Placing the VMs in multiple subnets of one virtual network removes the need for the load balancer.
The load balancer holds the listener IP address on the one cluster node that needs it at a time, the primary replica.

SQL-VM-1 and SQL-VM-2 sit in different availability zones as replicas with synchronous commit and automatic failover. They are nodes of one Windows Server failover cluster that needs an Active Directory
domain, so a domain controller VM is part of the design.

The replica in the remote region runs with asynchronous commit and manual failover. The two virtual networks are joined by virtual network peering or a site-to-site VPN gateway, and replication between

Azure Backup installs the AzureBackupWindowsWorkload extension on each SQL Server VM. It streams backups through SQL native APIs straight to the Recovery Services vault with no staging location, honours
the availability group backup preference, and can take log backups as often as every 15 minutes.
The cloud witness gives the cluster a quorum vote, so a two-node cluster can keep running with one node online. It needs a Standard general-purpose v2 storage account with locally redundant storage;
Premium storage is not supported for a cloud witness.
Site Recovery replicates the app tier VM to Region 2. The web and app tiers fail over only after the database failover is done. The Recovery Services vault used by Site Recovery holds metadata, not

A Site Recovery recovery plan runs the ASR-SQL-FailoverAG script from Azure Automation as the pre-action of its first group, which fails over the availability group before the app tier starts. This assumes
a domain controller already exists in the secondary region.
